groundTruth.cause: The local disk on one cluster node filled up, so map tasks running there could not write their output (no valid local directory) and had to be killed and re-run on other nodes.
keyEvidence: Could not find any valid local directory
goodNextSteps: Check free disk space on the node's YARN local directories (df on yarn.nodemanager.local-dirs)
Check which node the failed attempts ran on and whether YARN marked its disks unhealthy

cases.title: WordCount map tasks killed after retries

groundTruth.cause: One cluster node was disconnected from the network, so tasks could not reach HDFS datanodes on it (NoRouteToHost) to read their input blocks and were killed after retries.
goodNextSteps: Check network connectivity to the datanode address in the errors (ping, routes, switch port, firewall)
Check the HDFS datanode report for dead or unreachable nodes

answer.summary: Map tasks in Hadoop MapReduce are failing due to network connectivity issues with HDFS data nodes, leading to task kills after retries.
missingEvidence: Network connectivity status between the map task nodes and the HDFS data nodes (172.22.149.145, 10.190.173.170) at the time of the incident, including routing tables and firewall rules.
HDFS configuration files (hdfs-site.xml) and node registration logs showing the history of address changes for msra-sa-41.

hypotheses.cause: A network route failure is preventing the MapReduce tasks from connecting to specific HDFS data nodes (e.g., 172.22.149.145 and 10.190.173.170), causing I/O errors and subsequent task kills.
hypotheses.nextStep: Verify network reachability from the map task nodes to the HDFS data nodes (172.22.149.145 and 10.190.173.170) using ping and telnet commands, and check routing tables and firewall configurations on the involved nodes.

hypotheses.cause: An address change in the HDFS client configuration (from msra-sa-41/10.190.173.170:9000 to msra-sa-41:9000) may have caused stale connections or failed handoffs, leading to socket timeouts and task kills.
hypotheses.nextStep: Inspect the hdfs-site.xml configuration and node registration logs for msra-sa-41 to verify if the address change was intentional, and whether it was properly propagated to all clients.
